objective: Implement and qualify optional workload-dependent Live request collection from the exact supported engine.
user_steering: Work toward 0.3.17 today and make the engine choose how to execute depending on its work.
hypothesis: Fixed coalescing delays charge isolated writes and can wait unnecessarily behind an already busy queue. A bounded collector can omit that wait at light load and at pressure while amortizing durable publication for small concurrent groups.
scope: Correctness and functionality only. No performance qualification or supported release follows trial105.

phases: latency: no deliberate wait for an isolated request or unknown publication cost
coalescing: 2..7 ready requests may wait using observed successful publication cost
pressure: at least8 ready requests drain immediately up to the original64-request cap
implementation.publication_cost_ewma: First successful nonempty publication initializes; subsequent observations move one eighth of the difference without overflow.
implementation.coalescing_delay: min(configured maximum, recent publication estimate divided by2). Default maximum2ms; accept0..20ms.
implementation.deadline: One deadline starts before inspecting ready siblings. Later arrivals never extend it. Disconnect drains without waiting.
implementation.diagnostics: Separate optional getter; phase counts, selected delay and publication estimate. Existing LiveStats and protocol contracts remain exact.
implementation.ownership: One existing writer, existing channel and owned Command vectors. No additional threads or per-request allocation/counter.

invariants: Archive publication, two sync_all calls, file format, receipts, source/WAL and queries remain byte-exact.
Snapshot publication precedes successful ACK. Validation conflict preserves original whole-group atomic rejection.
Queue256, payload64MiB, group64, batch10K and delay ceiling20ms remain unchanged.
Existing compaction threshold64 and original full reclaim every32 inserted groups remain unchanged.
Prepared/confirmed retries, poison/unknown outcomes, pinned snapshots, exclusive lease and last-owner drain/join remain intact.
Feature-disabled original runtime paths remain exact apart from benchmark-only shutdown methods.
No benchmark names, offered rates, data keys, environment tuning hooks, dependency or supported version change.
required_checks: Fresh locked offline baseline and candidate full debug/release suites; strict default/adaptive/fault/benchmark lint configurations.
Deterministic collector tests for sparse/concurrent/pressure/disconnect/64-cap/arrival transition/zero-and-max delay and EWMA overflow.
Actual Live adaptive constructor, concurrent named and anonymous ACKs, pinned readers, reopen, collisions, prepared retries, queue and shape budgets.
Fresh relevant I/O-error and owned-process-exit publication schedules across all seven original cut points; reconcile acknowledged and ambiguous outcomes.
Independent full data/metadata CRC/index checks, SQLite references, old0.3.16 cross-open and byte equivalence where group boundaries match.
Reject malformed/corrupted/truncated stores. Preserve all failed sources, builds, commands, stdout/stderr, process identities and test stores.
Exact complete local preservation and independently replayed restored audit without Native or timer reruns.
future_performance: Use a new number106 or later with a predeclared balanced same-D repeated baseline A/A and fixed complete native/service gates before timers. Complete104 exact preservation/restore and evidence recording before new timers. Trial104 remains rejected in its complete scope. No optional adaptive mode or default change is adopted without the relevant integrated release checks.

research.use: Concurrency-dependent amortization; excessive waiting can worsen throughput and latency; natural grouping at high load.
Only concurrent work can justify commit delay. Synchronous durability is retained.
Nonblocking try_recv and disconnect-aware bounded recv_timeout; use APIs supported by local Rust1.97.1.
Research motivation for greedy drain at high load; external models are not Kestrel measurements or proof of this controller.
